title: Winter (La Frileuse)
description: Houdon personifies winter as a standing woman who folds herself into a shawl. The compact pose turns the contrast between cold bronze and softly modeled skin into the central subject. This bronze was cast by Houdon in 1787.

title: Night
description: A seated woman folds her arms across her knees and lowers her head into them. Maillol gives the enclosed pose a weight and stillness that change as the sculpture is seen from the side or back. His wife Clotilde was the model.
attribution: Night by Aristide Maillol. The Metropolitan Museum of Art. 3D scan by Polytech, via Polycam, CC BY 4.0. Packaged as GLB by Atrium; geometry and textures unchanged.
visual_qa: Source thumbnail inspected; full model renderer review is required before publishing.
content_review: Historical figurative sculpture in an art-historical context; adult figure, no sexual act.
artwork_rights: Reasoned public-domain assessment for the 1902–1909 composition, distinct from the museum photograph. Maillol died in 1944; French economic rights expired after 70 years (2015). The composition was publicly unveiled in 1909 according to the National Museum of Western Art. Met image itself is not marked public domain and is not used in the acquired scan.
rights_caveat: Met API isPublicDomain=false; that flag is disclosed, not treated as a scan license. Exact bronze casting date remains unknown. French wartime extensions ordinarily fall inside the harmonized 70-year term under the cited Cour de cassation ruling. No claim is made that the Met licensed this independent community scan.
object_identity: Public capture GPS and placemark identify the Metropolitan Museum. Pose and title match the museum record. Prefer this capture to Polytech F7D011FD-A957-4FEB-8E72-AC67E7E61AF9, which was captured in Pittsburgh and labeled 1939.
qa_notes: Figure appears complete in the source thumbnail, but the scanned base has visible holes near the feet; inspect whether these are acceptable in the final viewer.

title: Undine Rising from the Waters
description: Ives shows the water spirit Undine emerging with both arms raised. Drapery clings to her body and gathers above her head, making the marble appear at once solid and translucent. This version belongs to the High Museum of Art in Atlanta.
attribution: Undine Rising from the Waters by Chauncey Bradley Ives. High Museum of Art. 3D scan by timmyjack, via Polycam, CC BY 4.0. Packaged as GLB by Atrium; geometry and textures unchanged.

artwork_rights: Historical nineteenth-century artwork by Ives (1810–1894); public-domain assessment based on dates.
object_identity: Public capture in Atlanta, close to High Museum. The scan thumbnail is a rear view with raised arms, drapery and round base. title: The Sluggard
description: Leighton captures a standing man stretching, with both arms bent beside his head. The relaxed gesture lengthens the torso while shifting the body off its central axis. This scan was made at the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
attribution: The Sluggard by Frederic, Lord Leighton. Royal Academy of Arts. 3D scan by Beto88, via Polycam, CC BY 4.0. Packaged as GLB by Atrium; geometry and textures unchanged.

content_review: Historical figurative sculpture in an art-historical context; adult figure, no sexual act.
artwork_rights: Historical sculpture exhibited in 1886 by Leighton (1830–1896); public-domain assessment based on dates.
object_identity: Capture title identifies Royal Academy and GPS is at Burlington Gardens. Composition is an exact match. The full-size Royal Academy plaster is 03/1765, 190 × 94 cm, dated 1885 in the cited research article with Royal Academy image credit.
